result.title: Event-based object detection under adverse lighting and motion: lessons for construction sites
result.summary: Vision-based monitoring on construction sites fails at night, at dawn and dusk, in tunnels and under floodlights, when conventional RGB cameras under- or over-expose. Event cameras record per-pixel brightness changes with microsecond latency and over 120 dB of dynamic range, but their benefit for site-relevant object detection has not been quantified on real data. We compare three recent event-based detectors (SMamba, SATE and EvRT-DETR) with an RGB detector trained on the same data, using the pixel-aligned PEOD dataset. On low-light frames (70% of the test set) the best event detector reaches 27.2 AP against 21.3 AP for RGB, and a training-free late fusion of both sensors is the best option in every lighting condition (33.3 AP). An object-level analysis of 53,091 objects shows that brightness has little effect on event detectors, whereas fast motion matters: above 20 pixels per frame RGB finds 11-19% of medium-size objects and EvRT-DETR 39-60%. Activation patching locates the damage caused by losing events at the 1/16-resolution features, with small objects depending on the finest scale, and shows that event detectors fail when few signal events meet added noise. A model-agnostic pruning study keeps about 95% of accuracy with 60% of the input but halves small-object recall. On rendered construction sites, used zero-shot, dimming the floodlights drops RGB to near zero while the event detector keeps most of its AP50. We close with camera-placement guidance for construction sites.

AI.brief_summary: 在像素对齐的 PEOD 数据集上比较三种事件相机检测器与 RGB 检测器，量化低光与快速运动下的检测收益，并显示无训练晚期融合在各光照条件下最优；另用激活路径修补与剪枝分析定位失效来源。
AI.relevance_reason: 事件相机本身与 LVR 无直接关联，但按特征尺度做激活修补、定位「信号事件被噪声淹没」与细粒度信息丢失位置的分析，可能可供核查多模态模型内部视觉细节在哪一层坍缩。
